change: LFSR_PARAM_CHECK: refuse an lfsr_crc whose params.poly / k_steps / n_inputs CONTRADICT its own matrix, instead of copying them into the report. The reconstruction is exact: a one-step Galois or Fibonacci companion is read straight off the matrix in stage coordinates (params.bit_order), and any declared (poly, k_steps) pair is checked by A == C^k or A == (C^k)^T. A value the harness cannot reconstruct or verify (a programmable polynomial, form 'affine', k_steps null with a matrix that is not one step) is marked unchecked, never assumed right. The lfsr's `form` is never a refusal. WHAT THE CHECK ACCEPTS, AND WHY IT IS WEAKER THAN IT LOOKS: the polynomial is compared up to its x^w bit AND up to REFLECTION (bit i = the coefficient of x^(w-i)), and the matrix up to the reversal of the stage order -- 8 candidate matrices. That is not a taste: the project carries BOTH conventions (tools/s3/lfsr.py's _poly_of against tools/s3/corpus.py's truth) and nothing in a netlist fixes which end of a stage chain is stage 0.

change: THE HOLD COVER IS READ OFF THE CUBES THE HARNESS CHECKED, NOT OFF THE CASE CONDs: HOLD_EMPTY_NEEDS_VERIFIED_COVER now runs TWO tests, not one. SUPERSEDES THE CONTRACT AS PV12 AND T09 STATE IT. Those entries say an empty hold region is accepted when the VERIFIED cases empty it BY THEMSELVES, decided by the single test (a) 'the same region without the load conjunct is unsatisfiable'. That test is NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT. A reset case is CHECKED only on its own priority cube, which conjoins ~(each load case), so the reset CONDs can empty the region at full size while the load-active part of each reset case was checked by nothing at all. The rewrite that exploits it (T2, out/s3/verify/hold_gate_t2.py) turns each literal of `when` into its own LYING reset case and hides the lie behind a load: for when = [l_1..l_k] whose ~l_r is the real synchronous reset, set reset := [{[~l_i], v} for i != r] + [{[~l_r], v}] and load := [[~l_i, l_r] for i != r]. Every lying case is then checked only inside the real reset, where it happens to be true; the reset CONDs cover ~when; test (a) passes; the structure verifies with ZERO hold obligations checked. THE RULE AS IT NOW SHIPS: an empty hold region is accepted, and reported as vacuous, only when BOTH (a) the region without the load conjunct is unsatisfiable AND (b) NO load case is satisfiable outside the defining cases. Both must answer unsat; 'sat' on either gives hold_vacuous_cover = 'load' and REFUSES the structure (the reason string says which test), and an undecided answer -- solver unknown or the conflict budget -- REFUSES it too, never assumed covered. Test (b) is vacuous when there are no load cases, so a free-running counter (when = []) and every load-free structure are bit-identical to before. NOT A TUNED THRESHOLD: it is a contract rule with one boolean (the same HOLD_EMPTY_NEEDS_VERIFIED_COVER switch PV12 introduced), and the boolean exists so the measurement below can be reproduced; there is no number to tune and none was. WHAT IT DOES NOT CLOSE, restated because it is the same caveat PV12 carries: the rule bounds the SHAPE of the cover, NOT ITS SIZE. A PARTIAL complement leaves the hold region non-empty on a sliver and the obligation is then genuinely checked -- on that sliver. lane_share['hold'] and load_hidden_share bound the size, reset_cases[i].share against lane_share['reset[i]'] bounds how far a NAMED CASE's value claim was narrowed below its printed COND, and none of the three is gated (a floor would be a tuned threshold and would need its own entry). THE DOCUMENTS ARE RECONCILED IN THIS SAME ENTRY: tools/s3/schema.py's control.hold note (an OUT_OF_SAMPLE_SOURCE, so the published holdout estimate was re-derived on this code state) and docs/S3_DESIGN.md section 3.7 both stated the one-test rule and now state the two-test rule in verify.py's words, together with what hold_vacuous_cover's four values assert ('verified' = both tests unsat; 'load' = one was sat, REFUSED; HOLD_COVER_UNDECIDED = the rule is off and load cases exist, so the question was not decided at all; 'unknown'/'budget' = a solver answer, REFUSED).
